Unlock Massive Savings on Wood County, Ohio’s Tax Deed Sale

Can you buy properties at 60% off market value in Ohio? Yes! At Wood County’s Sheriff’s Delinquent Tax Sales, bidders buy properties below market value and wipe out previous mortgages. With a population of about 133,000, Wood County, home to Bowling Green, offers more than scenic beauty.

Understanding Tax Lien Certificates and Tax Deeds:

The county sells tax lien certificates when property owners fail to pay their taxes. Investors pay the outstanding taxes and, in return, receive a lien on the property. If the property owner doesn’t repay the taxes plus interest, the investor can foreclose on the property. On the other hand, tax deeds involve buying the property outright at a tax sale auction, wiping out previous liens and mortgages. Both methods can offer substantial returns compared to traditional investments.

Pro Tips:

  • Do Your Research: Always check the property for any existing liens or encumbrances.
  • Understand the Process: Familiarize yourself with the bidding process on the Realauction website.
  • Budget for Additional Costs: Prepare to cover costs, allowances, and taxes that go beyond the sale proceeds.

Attractions and Economic Highlights in Wood County:

  • Popular Attractions: Wood County is home to beautiful parks, theatres, and historic sites.
  • Transportation Infrastructure: The county connects to major roads and rails and provides access to airports.
  • Economic Development: The county has growing sectors in agriculture, technology, and manufacturing.
  • Community Appeal: Enjoy outdoor recreational activities, entertainment options, and eco-tourism opportunities.

FAQs:

  1. Can I inspect the properties before the sale?
    • No, buyers purchase properties “as-is” without any opportunity for inspection.
  2. What happens if there is no buyer at the first auction?
    • A second sale is held with no minimum bid, where true opportunities might arise.
  3. Are there any warranties on the properties?
    • No, all sales are “buyer beware,” and no warranties are expressed or implied.

For more details and current listings, check the Wood County Sheriff’s Office and Realauction.
